paragraphs: Human preference data often says which of two behavior segments is preferred without recording how strongly one is preferred. This leaves reward learning with an important ambiguity: a close choice and an obvious choice can receive the same kind of ranking label. The paper introduces an adaptive preference loss to account for this missing information about preference strength.

The loss is grounded in distributionally robust optimization and assigns a separate scaling parameter to each pair. Ambiguous pairs receive smaller scales, encouraging similar rewards, while clearer preferences receive larger scales, encouraging greater reward separation. For each scaling parameter, the optimization problem is strictly convex and involves only one variable, allowing an efficient second-order optimization procedure.

The method can also be incorporated into other preference optimization frameworks, including direct preference optimization. Experiments in robotic control and language generation report improved policy performance. They also indicate that reward-function selection becomes more closely aligned with policy optimization, simplifying hyperparameter tuning. These findings support treating preference strength as something to adapt during learning rather than assuming that every ranking conveys equally decisive evidence.
neurips-2024-adaptive-preference-scaling.tldr: An adaptive preference loss adjusts reward differences to reflect ambiguous versus clear preferences, improving policy learning in robotic control and language-generation experiments.

paragraphs: Predicting processes that vary across space and time is difficult when observations are scarce or unevenly distributed. Expensive sensor deployment can worsen these imbalances, while highly customized models can struggle to generalize. CaPaint addresses this problem through a causal framework that identifies relevant regions in the data and seeks to give prediction models a basis for causal reasoning.

The approach first distinguishes causal regions from regions treated as environmental or non-causal. It then uses back-door adjustment together with diffusion-based inpainting to address those environmental regions. A fine-tuned unconditional diffusion model fills the corresponding masks, supplying generated variations of the surrounding context. This offers a possible route to extrapolation across potential data distributions.

The paper reports reducing data-generation complexity from exponential to quasi-linear relative to the optimal spatio-temporal causal discovery models it discusses. Across five real-world benchmarks, incorporating CaPaint produces reported improvements ranging from 4.3% to 77.3%. These results support the usefulness of combining causal region identification with generative augmentation, while the abstract presents reliable extrapolation as a possibility rather than a universal guarantee.
neurips-2024-causal-deciphering-and-inpa.tldr: CaPaint combines causal region identification with diffusion inpainting to augment spatio-temporal data and improve prediction across five benchmarks.

paragraphs: Averaging probability distributions requires deciding what it means for their contents to be close. Optimal transport barycenters provide a geometry-aware answer, using transport costs to define the average. This paper develops an algorithm for approximating continuous entropic optimal transport barycenters with arbitrary transport cost functions, broadening the kinds of geometry that the averaging procedure can represent.

The algorithm starts from a dual reformulation based on weak optimal transport. This reformulation connects barycenter estimation to the training of energy-based models, allowing established learning procedures from that area to serve the averaging task. The authors also establish bounds on the quality of the recovered solution and provide an optimization scheme that avoids min-max optimization and other complicated estimation machinery.

The evaluation covers low-dimensional examples and image-space settings, including non-Euclidean costs. The paper additionally studies barycenters restricted to an image manifold produced by a pretrained generative model. Together, these demonstrations explore how a mathematically defined distributional average can be computed in both simple spaces and structured image spaces, with flexibility in the cost used to express similarity.
neurips-2024-energy-guided-continuous-en.tldr: The paper connects continuous entropic transport barycenter estimation to energy-based learning, supporting arbitrary costs and providing solution-quality bounds.

paragraphs: FreeSplat aims to reconstruct indoor scenes from long image sequences so that they can be viewed from a broad range of positions. Existing generalizable Gaussian splatting methods are described as largely limited to interpolation within narrow ranges between stereo images. The paper connects this limitation to heavy feature-processing backbones and difficulty accurately placing the scene's 3D Gaussians.

Its first component gathers information across nearby views using adaptive cost volumes and a multiscale feature structure. Pixel-wise Triplet Fusion then combines observations from multiple views while removing redundant Gaussians where views overlap. A separate training strategy prepares the model for wider viewpoint changes across different numbers of input images. These components address both scene consistency and the cost of combining many observations.

Experiments report state-of-the-art rendered color quality and depth accuracy across varying input-view counts. FreeSplat also performs inference more efficiently and reduces redundant Gaussians. The findings support broader-view reconstruction from sequences, while the authors frame feed-forward reconstruction of large scenes without depth priors as a possibility opened by the approach.
neurips-2024-freesplat-generalizable-3d-.tldr: FreeSplat combines information across long image sequences and removes redundant Gaussians to improve efficient, geometrically consistent synthesis over wider viewpoints.

paragraphs: A graph foundation model needs patterns that remain useful when the task or application domain changes. The paper identifies the choice of a transferable vocabulary as a central obstacle: graphs do not come with an obvious equivalent of reusable text tokens. GFT proposes computation trees as the units from which such a vocabulary can be built.

These trees are derived from the message-passing process used to exchange information across a graph. By treating the resulting structures as tokens, GFT represents graphs through patterns associated with how information is gathered and combined. The intended benefit is a shared representation that helps transfer across tasks and domains while reducing negative transfer, where knowledge carried from one setting harms another.

The paper provides theoretical analyses and extensive experiments supporting the transferability of computation trees and the effectiveness of GFT across diverse graph-learning settings. Its contribution is therefore both a model and a proposal for what a reusable graph vocabulary should contain. The reported findings support computation trees as useful transferable patterns without establishing them as the only possible foundation for graph models.
neurips-2024-gft-graph-foundation-model-.tldr: GFT uses computation trees from graph message passing as reusable tokens to improve transfer across graph-learning tasks and domains.

paragraphs: Harmony4D addresses the difficulty of understanding people who interact closely, including situations where their bodies overlap or obscure one another. Earlier interaction datasets are described as relying heavily on choreographed activities in controlled indoor environments. This dataset broadens the setting with activities such as wrestling, dancing, and mixed martial arts captured across diverse environments.

A flexible system of more than 20 synchronized cameras records the interactions. The dataset contains 208 video sequences, 24 subjects, 1.66 million images, and 3.32 million human instances. Its annotations support detection, tracking, pose estimation in two and three dimensions, and body-mesh recovery. A markerless tracking algorithm handles severe occlusion and close interaction to produce these annotations with minimal manual intervention.

Evaluations expose substantial limitations in existing mesh-recovery methods when people are in close contact. Fine-tuning a pretrained HMR2.0 model on Harmony4D yields a reported 54.8% improvement in PVE for scenes with severe occlusion and contact. The dataset consequently serves both as a demanding evaluation resource and as training material that improves performance in the interaction conditions it targets.
neurips-2024-harmony4d-a-video-dataset-f.tldr: Harmony4D provides richly annotated multiview videos of close human interactions, exposing reconstruction weaknesses and improving a model fine-tuned on its data.

paragraphs: Stochastic compositional optimization studies objectives built by composing functions, with applications ranging from AUC maximization to vertical federated learning. Some settings provide derivatives directly, while black-box settings require their estimation. This paper asks how losing access to derivatives changes the learning guarantees of two optimization algorithms, SCGD and SCSC.

The analysis first develops a new stability framework that gives sharper generalization upper bounds in convex settings under some milder conditions. It then extends the reasoning to non-convex objectives using a property of smooth functions called almost co-coercivity. Combining this framework with optimization analysis produces learning guarantees for three black-box variants of non-convex SCGD and SCSC.

Comparing the bounds reveals that better gradient estimation yields tighter learning guarantees. It also shows that a larger proportion of unknown gradients may increase dependence on estimation quality. The authors apply the analysis to FOO-based vertical VFL and VFL-CZOFO, establishing learning guarantees consistent with these findings. The contribution clarifies theoretically how the quality and extent of missing derivative information affect what these methods can guarantee.
neurips-2024-how-does-black-box-impact-t.tldr: The paper derives black-box compositional optimization guarantees showing how gradient-estimation quality and the proportion of unknown gradients affect learning bounds.

paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders try to explain neural-network activations using a large collection of features, only a few of which are active for any input. Reconstructing activations accurately, however, provides only indirect evidence that those features matter to the network's computation. The paper argues that conventional training may capture structure in the dataset more strongly than structure responsible for the model's behavior.

End-to-end sparse dictionary learning changes the training objective to focus on the model's outputs. It inserts the autoencoder's reconstructed activations into the network and minimizes the KL divergence between the resulting output distribution and the original model's distribution. This makes preserving the network's behavior the direct criterion for learning functionally important features.

Compared with standard sparse autoencoders, the authors report a Pareto improvement: more network performance is explained using fewer total features and fewer active features per input, without a loss of interpretability. They also examine geometric and qualitative differences between the learned dictionaries. The findings support using downstream behavior to train more concise explanations of network computation, rather than relying solely on activation reconstruction.
neurips-2024-identifying-functionally-im.tldr: Training sparse autoencoders to preserve model outputs produces more compact, functionally relevant feature dictionaries without a reported loss of interpretability.

paragraphs: Gloss-free sign language translation avoids the costly gloss annotations used by other translation systems, but its performance still trails gloss-based approaches. This paper identifies a possible bottleneck in the visual representations learned by gloss-free models. Gestures with different meanings can occupy closely packed positions in feature space, making them difficult for the model to distinguish.

SignCL addresses this representation-density problem through self-supervised contrastive learning. The training strategy encourages more discriminative visual features, helping the model separate semantically distinct gestures. Because it changes the learning strategy without increasing the model's parameter count, its reported gains do not require enlarging the translation model.

Experiments show reduced representation density and improved translation across multiple frameworks. On CSL-Daily, the reported BLEU improvements are 39% for the Sign Language Transformer and 46% for GFSLT-VLP. SignCL also outperforms Sign2GPT while using 35% of its parameters. These results support representation separation as a useful intervention across the evaluated systems, while the paper presents density as a potential bottleneck rather than the sole explanation for gloss-free translation's performance gap.
neurips-2024-improving-gloss-free-sign-l.tldr: SignCL improves gloss-free sign language translation by using contrastive learning to separate crowded gesture representations without adding model parameters.

paragraphs: Diffusion models progressively transform data into noise before learning a reverse process for generation. Existing theoretical analyses of variance-exploding models have slower forward convergence guarantees than those for variance-preserving models. The paper attributes this gap to the absence of drift in the Brownian forward process and introduces a drifted variance-exploding stochastic differential equation.

The new process reaches an exponential forward convergence rate in diffusion time. Under the manifold hypothesis, the authors establish efficient polynomial sample complexity for a series of variance-exploding models using reverse stochastic differential equations. Their analysis also permits an unbounded diffusion coefficient, making the setting closer to the state-of-the-art models discussed in the paper.

A unified tangent-based framework covers both stochastic reverse processes and deterministic probability-flow ordinary differential equations. It yields a quantitative convergence guarantee for state-of-the-art variance-exploding models using the deterministic reverse process. Synthetic and real-world experiments additionally show that the drifted process can balance error terms and improve generated samples without training. The work combines conditional theoretical guarantees with empirical evidence for the practical value of modifying the forward dynamics.
neurips-2024-leveraging-drift-to-improve.tldr: Adding drift to variance-exploding diffusion enables faster theoretical convergence, conditional sample-complexity guarantees, and empirical sample improvements without training.

paragraphs: Promptable segmentation usually needs a separate manual prompt for each object. Task-generic prompting instead starts with one instruction that applies across images, using a multimodal language model to derive object-specific guidance. The difficulty is that the derived prompts can contain hallucinations, making them unreliable instructions for the segmentation model.

ProMaC treats those hallucinations as potential sources of contextual information that must subsequently be checked and refined. Its prompt generator uses multiscale chain-of-thought prompting to produce extended contextual prompts, then reduces inaccuracies to obtain more precise instance-specific instructions. A mask generator uses these instructions and semantic alignment to produce regions consistent with the task.

The two generators operate in an iterative cycle. Generated masks direct subsequent prompting toward task-relevant image regions, helping reduce irrelevant hallucinations and improve both prompts and masks. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The central idea is a staged use of broader pretrained knowledge: initially expand the contextual information considered, then use verification and segmentation feedback to focus that information on the image and task.
neurips-2024-leveraging-hallucinations-t.tldr: ProMaC iteratively checks and refines hallucination-derived context through prompt and mask generation to reduce reliance on object-specific manual prompts.

paragraphs: Recovering a three-dimensional human pose from a two-dimensional input is ambiguous because depth is not directly observed. The paper provides theoretical and empirical evidence that traditional regression models can consequently produce poses with inconsistent topology. It also argues that standard metrics such as MPJPE, P-MPJPE, and PCK do not assess this particular problem.

ManiPose represents the ambiguity explicitly by producing multiple candidate 3D poses and estimating the plausibility of each. It constrains every candidate to lie on the human pose manifold, a space representing consistent human poses. Within this construction, the method guarantees consistency of its candidate poses. It also avoids the generative models used by earlier multi-hypothesis approaches, simplifying training and use.

On real-world datasets, ManiPose substantially improves pose consistency compared with state-of-the-art models while remaining very competitive on MPJPE. These findings highlight a distinction between matching measured joint positions and producing a structurally consistent body pose. The approach addresses both by retaining multiple depth interpretations while constraining each interpretation to respect the pose structure.
neurips-2024-manipose-manifold-constrain.tldr: ManiPose handles depth ambiguity with multiple plausibility-scored 3D poses constrained to remain structurally consistent.

paragraphs: MVSplat360 generates new views around real-world scenes from a small set of input images. This is difficult because sparse views may overlap very little and leave much of the scene unobserved. The paper describes the problem as inherently ill-posed: the available images do not provide enough visual information to determine every requested view.

The method combines geometry-aware reconstruction with temporally consistent video generation. A modified feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting model renders features directly into the latent space of a pretrained Stable Video Diffusion model. Those features supply pose and appearance cues for denoising, guiding the generation of photorealistic views that remain consistent with the reconstructed 3D scene. The full system supports end-to-end training.

The authors report arbitrary-view rendering with as few as five sparse input views. They introduce a benchmark based on DL3DV-10K, where MVSplat360 achieves better visual quality than state-of-the-art methods on wide camera sweeps and full 360-degree synthesis. Results on RealEstate10K also support the method's effectiveness, demonstrating the value of combining explicit geometry with video-generation capabilities in this sparse-observation setting.
neurips-2024-mvsplat360-feed-forward-360.tldr: MVSplat360 guides video diffusion with reconstructed 3D features to synthesize consistent wide-ranging views from as few as five input images.

paragraphs: Generative Flow Networks learn to construct objects through sequences of state transitions, with the aim of sampling objects in proportion to their rewards. The paper observes that training on too few trajectories can leave valuable objects underused. In particular, the flow estimated for an object may differ substantially from its already known reward.

The proposed pessimistic backward policy, PBP-GFN, addresses that mismatch by maximizing the observed flow so that it aligns more closely with the object's true reward. The intervention targets how the model learns from construction trajectories. Its motivation is that identifying a high-reward object is not enough if the learned flow still assigns it insufficient weight during sampling.

The authors evaluate the method on eight benchmarks: a hyper-grid environment, bag generation, structured set generation, molecular generation, and four RNA sequence generation tasks. They report improved discovery of high-reward objects, preserved object diversity, and consistently better performance than existing methods across these evaluations. The results suggest that improving flow alignment can strengthen reward-seeking behavior while retaining the diversity central to the sampling objective.
neurips-2024-pessimistic-backward-policy.tldr: PBP-GFN brings observed flow closer to known rewards, improving high-reward object discovery while preserving diversity across eight benchmarks.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning combines labeled and unlabeled examples, but successful methods for classification do not transfer directly to regression. Classification predicts categories, whereas regression predicts numerical values. RankUp creates a connection between these settings by adding a ranking problem alongside the original numerical prediction task.

The auxiliary ranking classifier produces classification outputs about ordering, making it compatible with existing semi-supervised classification techniques. The model trains this task concurrently with the regression objective, so learning from rankings supports the original prediction problem. The paper also introduces regression distribution alignment, which improves pseudo-labels through distribution alignment. These pseudo-labels provide training targets where original labels are unavailable.

Across regression benchmarks in computer vision, audio, and natural language processing, RankUp achieves reported state-of-the-art results both with and without the additional alignment technique. Distribution alignment further improves its performance. The contribution is a simple way to reuse advances in semi-supervised classification for numerical prediction: supply a related categorical task that can benefit from those methods while continuing to optimize the regression output directly.
neurips-2024-rankup-boosting-semi-superv.tldr: RankUp trains an auxiliary ranking classifier alongside regression to bring semi-supervised classification methods to numerical prediction.

paragraphs: Diffusion transformers can produce high-quality outputs, but large models impose substantial training and inference costs. RemixDiT explores whether different denoising timesteps can benefit from specialized experts without requiring a separately trained transformer for every expert. Its goal is to improve generation quality through specialization at a lower cost than training many independent models.

The method starts with K basis models and learns mixing coefficients that construct N experts, where K is smaller than N. These mixtures adapt model capacity to different denoising timesteps. Although storing the collection increases total model size, each constructed expert retains the architecture of a standard diffusion transformer. This preserves the computational form of the model used for denoising.

Experiments on ImageNet report promising results relative to standard diffusion transformers and other multiple-expert methods. The findings support learned model mixing as a way to obtain timestep-specific behavior without independently training every expert. The efficiency claim concerns the mixed model's standard architecture; the paper explicitly acknowledges that the overall collection of model parameters is larger.
neurips-2024-remix-dit-mixing-diffusion-.tldr: RemixDiT learns to mix a smaller set of basis models into timestep-specific diffusion experts, improving generation while retaining a standard expert architecture.

paragraphs: Reliable prediction requires both a useful point estimate and an informative account of uncertainty. Self-Calibrating Conformal Prediction combines these goals by producing calibrated point predictions together with prediction intervals. Its interval guarantee has a specific conditioning target: finite-sample validity conditional on the calibrated predictions, rather than validity conditional on every input feature.

The method combines Venn-Abers calibration with conformal prediction, extending the original Venn-Abers procedure from binary classification to regression. The accompanying theory handles calibration and interval construction on the same data. It also accommodates cases where the conditioning set or the scores used to construct intervals depend on the calibrated predictions themselves.

Experiments on real data show improved interval efficiency through model calibration. This matters because the point prediction and its uncertainty interval are designed as connected outputs, with the calibration step helping the interval procedure. The authors present the approach as a practical alternative to feature-conditional validity. Its contribution is therefore a particular, prediction-conditional guarantee and a framework for obtaining it while reusing the calibration data.
neurips-2024-self-calibrating-conformal-.tldr: The method combines calibrated regression predictions with finite-sample-valid intervals conditional on those predictions, improving interval efficiency in real-data experiments.

paragraphs: Structured pruning reduces a language model's size by removing organized components, but retaining performance under tight computational budgets remains difficult. SlimGPT proposes a fast, low-cost pruning method based on the Optimal Brain Surgeon framework. It focuses on choosing removals carefully enough to limit the damage introduced during compression.

Its Batched Greedy Pruning procedure combines two mechanisms. Grouped Cholesky decomposition improves estimates of the error caused by pruning attention heads, while Dynamic Group Size makes pruning feed-forward networks more efficient. The authors report obtaining approximately locally optimal pruning results within one hour. This is a claim about the pruning procedure's reported results, rather than a guarantee of a globally best compressed model.

The paper also examines how errors accumulate when layers are pruned separately. Its Incremental Pruning Ratio strategy varies pruning across layers to reduce performance degradation. On the LLaMA benchmark, SlimGPT outperforms other methods and achieves reported state-of-the-art results. Together, the contributions address both the immediate quality of component-removal decisions and the accumulated effect of those decisions across the model.
neurips-2024-slimgpt-layer-wise-structur.tldr: SlimGPT combines efficient component selection with nonuniform layer pruning to compress language models while reducing accumulated performance loss.

paragraphs: Professional data workflows require more than writing an isolated query or script. They span stages such as warehousing and orchestration, and often combine code with graphical interfaces. Spider2-V evaluates whether multimodal agents can carry out these broader workflows in authentic computer environments using enterprise data software.

The benchmark contains 494 tasks and incorporates 20 professional applications. Tasks require agents to write code and operate interfaces, reflecting real-world use cases. The authors provide automatic task configuration, carefully designed task-specific evaluation metrics, and extensive software documentation. These resources make realistic workflows more practical to set up and evaluate while giving agents access to relevant application knowledge.

The evaluated state-of-the-art agents achieve only 14.0% success on full workflows. Even with step-by-step guidance, reported success remains low for fine-grained, knowledge-intensive interface actions at 16.2% and remote cloud workspaces at 10.6%. These results identify a substantial gap between individual model capabilities and reliable workflow automation. Spider2-V supplies a benchmark for measuring progress on that gap in professional data settings.
neurips-2024-spider2-v-how-far-are-multi.tldr: Spider2-V evaluates agents on 494 professional data tasks and finds that existing systems rarely complete full workflows reliably.

paragraphs: A language agent's performance at deployment does not reveal how well it can improve through experience. The paper identifies this as a gap in existing benchmarks, which primarily measure capabilities already present in the model. StreamBench instead evaluates whether agents can become more effective as they encounter a sequence of inputs and feedback.

The benchmark simulates an online learning environment with a continuing feedback stream. Agents can use that experience to iteratively improve their performance, making adaptation over time the central object of evaluation. This setup connects the assessment to a post-deployment question: how well can an agent turn feedback from its ongoing work into better subsequent behavior?

Alongside the benchmark, the authors propose several simple, effective improvement baselines and analyze the components that contribute to successful streaming strategies. The contribution is both an evaluation setting and an initial set of methods for studying adaptation within it. The paper positions StreamBench as a foundation for developing stronger online learning strategies, rather than presenting continuous improvement as a capability already solved for deployed language agents.
neurips-2024-streambench-towards-benchma.tldr: StreamBench evaluates how language agents improve through a continuing stream of inputs and feedback, with baselines and analysis of successful adaptation strategies.

paragraphs: Understanding an image involves recognizing relationships as well as objects. Research has often treated human-object interaction detection, scene graph generation, and referring relationships as separate tasks. FleVRS brings these related problems into a single visual relationship segmentation model, aiming to provide a more cohesive way to identify and localize relationships in images.

The model supports both standard and promptable relationship segmentation, and it can operate with an open vocabulary to accommodate novel scenarios. It combines image information with text, using textual features from vision-language models to support visual concept understanding. This shared use of the two modalities allows the framework to ground different kinds of relationships within an image.

Experiments across datasets report improvements over existing models in standard, promptable, and open-vocabulary settings. Examples include gains of 1.9 mAP on HICO-DET, 11.4 Acc on VRD, and 4.7 mAP on unseen HICO-DET. These findings support the usefulness of a common framework across the evaluated relationship tasks, including settings that require handling previously unseen visual relationship categories.
neurips-2024-towards-flexible-visual-rel.tldr: FleVRS unifies several visual relationship tasks in one text-and-image model supporting standard, promptable, and open-vocabulary segmentation.

paragraphs: Clinical time series can be irregularly sampled and contain stochastic variation. Neural stochastic differential equations model such behavior by using neural networks for the drift and diffusion terms governing change over time. However, existing training algorithms require backpropagation through these dynamics, which the paper identifies as a major obstacle to stable and scalable learning.

Trajectory Flow Matching adapts flow matching from generative modeling to train these time-series models without simulation-based backpropagation through the dynamics. The authors establish necessary conditions for the method to learn time-series data and introduce a reparameterization trick that improves training stability. The necessary conditions characterize requirements for learning; they are not presented as an unconditional guarantee that learning will succeed.

The method is then adapted to clinical time series and evaluated on four datasets. Results show improvements in both overall predictive performance and uncertainty prediction. The latter matters because a model's estimate of how uncertain it is forms an important part of its output in this setting. The contribution connects a different training procedure with empirical gains in modeling both trajectories and their uncertainty.
neurips-2024-trajectory-flow-matching-wi.tldr: Trajectory Flow Matching trains neural stochastic differential equations without backpropagating through simulated dynamics and improves performance and uncertainty prediction on four clinical datasets.

paragraphs: Motion measurements from phones and wearables can reveal human activities, but models often generalize poorly when device placement, orientation, or activity changes. Privacy and security concerns also make large training datasets difficult to assemble. UniMTS introduces a unified pretraining procedure designed to address these sources of variation together.

The method uses contrastive learning to align motion time series with text descriptions enriched by language models, helping it learn activity semantics. To obtain training signals without a large motion-sensor dataset, it synthesizes time series from existing motion skeleton data covering all joints. Spatio-temporal graph networks capture relationships across joints, while rotation-invariant augmentation addresses changes in device mounting orientation.

Across 18 motion time-series classification benchmarks, the authors report improvements over the best baselines of 340% in zero-shot, 16.3% in few-shot, and 9.2% in full-shot settings. These findings support the combination of semantic alignment, skeleton-derived data, and orientation handling as a route to broader transfer. The evaluation spans different amounts of task-specific supervision, showing benefits beyond the usual practice of training and testing within one dataset.
neurips-2024-unimts-unified-pre-training.tldr: UniMTS combines skeleton-derived motion data, text alignment, graph modeling, and rotation augmentation to improve activity recognition across devices and datasets.

paragraphs: Video frame interpolation generates intermediate images between existing frames. Doing this well requires exchanging information across frames to understand motion. The paper argues that convolution-based approaches can have insufficient receptive fields, while attention-based approaches can be computationally expensive. VFIMamba instead uses selective state space models, which provide data-dependent sequence modeling with linear complexity.

Its Mixed-SSM Block interleaves tokens from adjacent frames before applying selective state space modeling in multiple directions. This arrangement lets information travel between the frames while retaining linear complexity. The authors also introduce a curriculum learning strategy that progressively develops the model's ability to handle inter-frame dynamics across different motion magnitudes.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, with particularly strong results at high resolution. On X-TEST, the reported improvements are 0.80 dB for 4K frames and 0.96 dB for 2K frames. The findings support both the architecture for efficient cross-frame information exchange and the training strategy for learning motion, especially in the high-resolution cases highlighted by the evaluation.
neurips-2024-vfimamba-video-frame-interp.tldr: VFIMamba interleaves neighboring-frame features in selective state space models to improve efficient video interpolation, especially at high resolutions.

paragraphs: The paper revisits whether LSTM-based language models can remain competitive when scaled using modern language-model design techniques. Its starting point is that Transformers overtook earlier LSTMs at scale, but established LSTM mechanisms may still be useful if their limitations are addressed. xLSTM changes both the gates controlling memory and the structure of memory itself.

The first change introduces exponential gating, accompanied by normalization and stabilization. The second produces two variants: sLSTM uses scalar memory, scalar updates, and new memory mixing, while mLSTM uses matrix memory with a covariance update rule and is fully parallelizable. These extensions are placed inside residual blocks, which are stacked to build the full xLSTM architectures.

The authors report that exponential gating and the revised memory structures allow xLSTM to compare favorably with state-of-the-art Transformers and state space models in performance and scaling. The contribution is therefore a concrete modernization of LSTM architectures for large-scale language modeling. The findings support their competitiveness in the reported comparisons, without asserting that one architecture is universally best across all language-modeling settings.
neurips-2024-xlstm-extended-long-short-t.tldr: xLSTM updates LSTM gating and memory structures to achieve favorable performance and scaling comparisons with Transformers and state space models.
